blocks.name: Reactions of Carboxylic Acids to Produce Acyl Chlorides

blocks.text: Reactions of Carboxylic Acids to Produce Acyl Chlorides

blocks.md:
- **Acyl chlorides **are compounds with the functional group -COCl
- They look similar in structure to **carboxylic acids **but have a Cl atom instead of an -OH group attached to the carbonyl (C=O)
- Acyl chlorides are **more reactive **than their corresponding carboxylic acids and are therefore often used as **starting materials **in the production of organic compounds such as **esters**
- They can be prepared from the reaction of carboxylic acids with:

  - **Solid **phosphorus(V) chloride (PCl<sub>5</sub>)
  - **Liquid **phosphorus(III) chloride (PCl<sub>3</sub>) and heat
  - **Liquid **sulfur dichloride oxide (SOCl<sub>2</sub>)
- For example, the acyl chloride **ethanoyl chloride **can be formed from **ethanoic acid **in the above reactions

blocks.text: Using ethanoic acid to form ethanoyl chloride

blocks.alt: Carboxylic Acids & Derivatives - Production of Acyl Chlorides, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes

blocks.md: ***Ethanoic acid can be used to produce ethanoyl chloride with different by-products depending on the reagent used***

- **Carboxylic acids **can be formed from the **oxidation** of primary alcohols
- The primary alcohols are firstly oxidised to **aldehydes **and then further oxidised to **carboxylic acids**
- Some carboxylic acids can get even **further oxidised**

- **Methanoic acid **is a **strong reducing agent** and gets **further oxidised **to **carbon dioxide** (CO<sub>2</sub>)
- The oxidation of methanoic acid can occur by:

  - Warming methanoic acid with **mild** **oxidising agents** such as **Fehling’s** or **Tollens’** reagent
  
    - In a Fehling’s solution, the Cu<sup>2+</sup> ion is **reduced **to Cu<sup>+</sup> ion which **precipitates **as **red **Cu<sub>2</sub>O
    - With Tollens’ reagent, the Ag<sup>+</sup> is **reduced **to Ag
  - Using **stronger **oxidising agents such as **acidified KMnO**<sub>**4**</sub>** **or **acidified K**<sub>**2**</sub>**Cr**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**<sub>**7**</sub>
  
    - The **purple **KMnO<sub>4</sub> solution turns **colourless **as Mn<sup>7+</sup> ions are **reduced **to Mn<sup>2+</sup> ions
    - The **orange** K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> solution turns **green **as the Cr<sup>6+</sup> ions are reduced to Cr<sup>3+</sup> ions

- Another carboxylic acid that can get further oxidised is **ethanedioic acid**
- A **strong oxidising agent **such as **warm acidified KMnO**<sub>**4**</sub>** **is required for the oxidation of ethanedioic acid to **carbon dioxide**
